title: Best Way to Bake Sourdough English Muffins
meta_description: Master the art of sourdough English muffins! Learn the best techniques for a perfect griddle crust and how to use a sourdough english muffins baking tray.
html:
There is nothing quite like the smell of toasted sourdough English muffins on a Saturday morning. Unlike the store-bought versions that often taste like cardboard, home-baked sourdough muffins have a complex tang and those coveted "nooks and crannies" that hold pools of melted butter perfectly.

The secret to success isn't just in the starter; it's in how you handle the dough during the final cook. While these are technically griddled, choosing the right sourdough english muffins baking tray or surface is critical to ensuring you don't end up with stuck dough or uneven browning.

Preparing Your Sourdough Dough

Start with a mature, active sourdough starter. You want a dough that is hydrated enough to be tacky but stable enough to hold its shape. Mix your flour, water, salt, and starter, then allow the dough to undergo a bulk fermentation until it has doubled in size. This slow rise is where the flavor develops.

Once fermented, shape your dough into small rounds, roughly 2-3 inches in diameter. Let these rounds proof on a flat surface for another hour. This second proof ensures the interior is airy and light, preventing the muffins from becoming dense hockey pucks.

Setting Up Your Sourdough English Muffins Baking Tray

Most people think of a skillet for English muffins, but if you are making a large batch, a preheated baking sheet on the stovetop or in the oven can be a game changer. However, sourdough is notorious for sticking to metal, especially when the sugars caramelize on the bottom.

To avoid the frustration of scrubbing burnt dough, I highly recommend using Silicone Baking Mats. These non-stick, reusable mats replace parchment and provide a consistent heat distribution across your sourdough english muffins baking tray. Because they are heat-resistant and non-stick, the muffins slide right off, and you get a professional, golden-brown finish without the sticky mess.

The Griddling Process

The key to that classic English muffin texture is low and slow heat. If your heat is too high, the outside burns before the center is cooked through.

  • Heat a small amount of butter or oil on your surface.
  • Place the proofed rounds on the heat, leaving space between them.
  • Cook for about 5-7 minutes per side.
  • Press down lightly with a spatula to ensure full contact with the heat source.
  • Flip only once you see small bubbles forming on the surface and the bottom is golden.

If you are using a baking tray in the oven to pre-set the shape before finishing them on the stove, Silicone Baking Mats ensure that the bottoms don't fuse to the metal during that initial heat blast.

Achieving the Perfect Nooks and Crannies

The "nooks and crannies" are actually the result of carbon dioxide bubbles expanding rapidly during the cooking process. To maximize these, avoid over-handling the dough after the final proof. If you flatten the muffins too much with a spatula, you'll crush those delicate air pockets.

Another tip is to ensure your starter is peak-activity. A sluggish starter won't produce enough gas, leading to a tighter crumb. If your muffins are coming out too dense, try a slightly longer bulk fermentation or increase your hydration by a tablespoon or two.

Cleanup and Storage

One of the biggest deterrents to baking sourdough is the cleanup. Between the floury counters and the sticky pans, it can be a chore. This is where the right gear makes a difference. Using Silicone Baking Mats means zero-scrub cleanup; you simply wipe them down or toss them in the sink, unlike parchment paper which ends up in the trash.

Once your muffins have cooled completely, store them in an airtight container or freeze them. Sourdough English muffins freeze beautifully. Just pop a frozen muffin directly into the toaster—no thawing required—for a breakfast that tastes fresh-baked.

FAQ

Why are my sourdough English muffins sticking to the pan?

Sticking usually happens because the pan isn't hot enough or you aren't using enough fat. To eliminate this entirely, use a non-stick surface or place Silicone Baking Mats on your tray to create a barrier between the dough and the metal.

Can I make these in an oven instead of on a stovetop?

Yes, you can bake them in the oven, but you will lose the characteristic griddled crust. If you go the oven route, use a sourdough english muffins baking tray lined with a silicone mat to ensure they don't stick to the bottom of the pan.

How long do homemade sourdough muffins last?

On the counter, they stay fresh for about 3-4 days. In the freezer, they can last up to 3 months. Always slice them with a serrated knife or a fork (to avoid squishing) before freezing for the best results.
